question: v05
q: Petrol's killing me. How much more am I paying than a year ago?

transcript.answer:
You're paying about **13.5% more for petrol than a year ago**, based on the ABS monthly CPI for August 2026, the latest release. That's more than three times overall inflation, which was **4.0%** over the same period.

In practice, a tank that cost $100 to fill in August 2025 cost about **$113.50** in August 2026.

**Most of the rise came in the last two months.** Prices have moved sharply this year:

| Month (2026) | Change from previous month | Change from a year earlier |
|---|---|---|
| March | **+32.8%** (a huge one-month spike) | +24.2% |
| April | −7.0% | +18.6% |
| May | −11.9% | +7.7% |
| June | −10.9% | −7.3% |
| July | +7.5% | −0.4% |
| August | **+14.8%** | **+13.5%** |

By June, the March spike had fully unwound, and petrol was actually cheaper than a year earlier. Then it jumped again: about **23% across July and August combined**. If it feels like it's suddenly got much worse, that's because it has.

These figures are averages across the eight capital cities, so your local servo may be a bit higher or lower. September's CPI should be out later this month and will show whether the rise kept going.
